newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson's SGS stake to fetch less than mkt price.
newsitem.headline: Thomson's SGS stake to fetch less than mkt price.

text.p: The sale of Thomson-CSF's stake in SGS-Thomson will not take place before April and will fetch less for parent Lagardere than the share valuation, a source close to the deal said on Monday.

As part of its buyout of Thomson SA, Lagardere wants to sell its 17.6 percent stake in semiconductor-maker SGS-Thomson, which is worth 6.8 billion francs at current market prices, which values the group at 40 billion.
The source said the group's condition at end-1996 would influence the sale price. The newspaper La Tribune Desfosses estimated the stake may be sold for four billion francs.

"The price will be below the share price. CEA-Industries and France Telecom will generate a nice capital gain by acquiring the shares at a lower price," the source said, but declined to give an amount.
Thomson-CSF, nuclear research specialist CEA-Industries and France Telecom are partners in a 1993 shareholder pact.
SGS-Thomson, listed in Paris and New York, earned $483.5 million in the first nine months, compared with $358.5 million for the year-earlier period.
